status_summary: No NNSA or DOE action ending Iran-related or United Nations-related nonproliferation activities was found. A CRS report of 2026-07-14 says NNSA's Nonproliferation and Arms Control subprogram supports verification and monitoring of Iranian nuclear capabilities and develops technology for International Atomic Energy Agency safeguards, and that the FY2027 request for Defense Nuclear Nonproliferation is $2.39 billion, with Global Material Security down 26 percent. The State Department announced on 2026-01-07 withdrawal from 66 international organizations under Executive Order 14199, but the sources read do not say whether any DOE nonproliferation work or the IAEA is affected.
title: End DOE nonproliferation activities involving Iran and the United Nations
uncertainties: Absence of evidence from a limited search. The researcher searched the everycrsreport.com NNSA budget report and ran general web searches on the IAEA and the 66-organization withdrawal; the reviewer re-read the CRS report and ran one web search on NNSA Iran and IAEA program cuts, which found no termination. The withdrawal list was not opened, so IAEA treatment is unknown; the withdrawal is not an NNSA action and is context only. The cut to Global Material Security is not tied by the report to Iran or UN work. The CRS report also notes that plutonium dilute-and-dispose work was halted under Executive Order 14302 in May 2025, which concerns disposition rather than Iran or UN activities.
